LH004 A historical propagation case

Retell the xz backdoor through activity, residue and propagation from the public record, noting which layer carried the first detectable signal and which LH F02 instrument would have recorded it. An essay in the Harbour standard's essay form with an annotated reading list, in studies/LH004/. Done when the essay exists with its reading list.

Work in the repository at /home/user/lighthouse. Follow AGENTS.md there. Commit the deliverable. When finished, report what you did, what could not be done, and the files you changed.

feedback.message: Wrote studies/LH004/: brief, essay in the Harbour essay form with Answer, Findings, Method, Limits, Next and Corrections, and an annotated reading list. First detected signal: activity on Andres Freund's machine on 29 March 2024 (S14), mapping to F02's processing surface; an earlier valgrind signal in Fedora's build infrastructure fits no F02 surface, a gap. The malicious tarballs were public from 24 February, undetected. Propagation ran through distribution build pipelines that neither GH Archive nor deps.dev watch. One fetch blocked (Ars Technica), one wrong URL corrected. Committed as 9650dba.

items.prompt:
LH003 Survey of surveys

Reading only. List the observatories that already exist, such as GH Archive, Cloudflare Radar, Software Heritage, Open Source Insights, OpenRouter's rankings and the vulnerability databases, with the layer each sees, its population, boundary, unit, cadence and licence, in studies/LH003/. Done when every candidate has a row or a reason for exclusion.

Work in the repository at /home/user/lighthouse. Follow AGENTS.md there. Commit the deliverable. When finished, report what you did, what could not be done, and the files you changed.

feedback.message: Wrote studies/LH003/: brief, sources.md with the survey table and a fetch log, and the write-up in the F05 skeleton. 34 candidates: 17 rows (GH Archive, Cloudflare AI Crawl Control and Radar, Software Heritage, deps.dev, OpenRouter rankings, CVE and NVD, OSV, GHSA, Anthropic Economic Index, OpenAI usage paper, Common Crawl, PyPI and npm download counts, Epoch AI, AI Incident Database, Hugging Face Hub) and 17 exclusions with reasons. Strongest finding: populations are almost disjoint by construction, no source states its overlap with another, none observes propagation directly. Fetches of NVD, cve.org and the Economic Index top page returned no content; several rows rest on search summaries and are flagged. Licence unconfirmed for eight sources. Per-instrument register entries left as a follow-up in Next. Committed as af3cf58.

I-0002 Sample the host

A sampler for the machine that claims dispatches: process activity, busy core seconds and requests per destination, at a stated interval, tagged as Lighthouse traffic. Post one sample per dispatch to Harbour as a resources feedback entry. Done when it has captured an idle baseline and one dispatch, with its own overhead measured.

Work in the repository at /home/user/lighthouse. Follow AGENTS.md there. Commit the deliverable. When finished, report what you did, what could not be done, and the files you changed.

feedback.message: Wrote harbour/sample.py, a standard-library sampler printing numeric fields named in harbour/requests.md (busyCoreSeconds over an interval, load, memory, swap, process count, established TCP connections, agentRssBytes, samplerCpuSeconds), with a local-only connectionsByRemote map under harbour/samples/. hb resources now posts its output. Calibration run harbour/samples/dispatch-I-0002.jsonl: 42 samples over 205 s during the task itself; overhead about 0.003 s of CPU per sample at a 5 s interval, about 0.035 s per one-shot call. Instrument record I-0002 appended to registers/instruments.md. Not measurable here: requests and bytes per destination; no IPv6 on this host. Committed as 4b7c69a.

harbour/hb export already pulls this workspace's issues, dispatches with their feedback, cost, north star and roadmap reports at the end of every session, stamped with a collection time and the Harbour commit. Write its instrument record in registers/instruments.md using the LH F05 form: what it detects, what it misses (the proxy audit log, proxy events, the driver's own tokens), how it was calibrated, its overhead, and the changes that would invalidate comparisons. The weekly cadence applies once Harbour is hosted. Done when the record exists.

items.issueTitle: I-0001 Register the export as an instrument

feedback.message: Wrote registers/instruments.md: preamble and the LH F05 instrument record for I-0001, describing cmd_export's five Harbour reads, the per-issue cost read, the file copy of roadmap and next-run session files, the redaction pass and the ticket status round-trip. Owner and retirement left blank with a note. Committed as 203b213. Found: export GETs check no status code; roadmap and next-run content is copied from session files rather than fetched; issues capped at 250 without pagination; redaction has never yet fired.
